newsitem.title: USA: Fort Howard to expand tissue capacity.
newsitem.headline: Fort Howard to expand tissue capacity.

text.p: Fort Howard Corp said Wednesday it will begin a $160 million construction project in 1997 at one of its U.S. mills to add tissue paper production capacity.

It will add capacity at either its Rincon, Ga., operation near Savannah or its plant in Muskogee, Okla. The decision will be based on access to markets, available labor, environmental permits and other factors.
About 100 full-time employees will be added to the workforce to support the new operations. Completion of construction is expected in 1999.
The company's share of the at-home tissue products market has grown to more than 11 percent in 1996 from four percent in 1985, it said.
The centerpiece of the expansion project will be a 270-inch paper machine and related wastepaper processing and converting operations.
Fort Howard said the project will create several hundred construction jobs during the building phase.
